title: Launch checklist — Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — GA
content:
Doc owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last reviewed with: Platform Control Plane (Ethan), Routing (Mina), Telemetry (Logan), SRE (Rafael), Console (Chloe), Security (Kaitlyn)

Purpose
- Single checklist for GA launch of Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools: flags, DB migrations/backfills, canary + enablement plan, monitoring, comms, and rollback.
- This is the “release train” view; detailed operational steps are in the Confluence runbook.

Definitions / components in scope
- Control plane: DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan model + APIs (create/update/promote/abort/hold/force-promote)
- Policy engine: gate evaluation v1 (latency/error/saturation + missing-data semantics)
- Routing/data plane: stage-based partition selection for Dedicated pools (multi-region aware)
- Telemetry: stage tags in metrics/traces + dashboards/alerts
- Console: timeline view + gate evidence retrieval + action availability (promote/abort/hold)
- Security/compliance: audit events for rollout actions + export/SIEM pipeline

Feature flags (authoritative list for GA)
- Flag naming here matches config repo conventions; confirm exact keys in prod config before go/no-go.

[ ] FF1: dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled
    - Master kill switch for all staged rollouts on Dedicated pools.
    - Expected default: OFF globally; ON for internal pools + allowlisted customer accounts/pools.

[ ] FF2: dedicated_staged_rollouts.control_plane_api
    - Enables create/update/get/list for rollout plans + promotion/abort/hold endpoints.
    - Expected default: ON in staging; ON in prod (guarded by authz and allowlist).

[ ] FF3: dedicated_staged_rollouts.routing_stage_partitioning
    - Enables stage-based traffic splitting / partition selection in routing.
    - Expected default: OFF in prod until canary.

[ ] FF4: dedicated_staged_rollouts.gate_eval_v1
    - Enables automated gate evaluation in policy engine.
    - Missing metrics behavior: FAIL-CLOSED (i.e., “Unknown” -> block promotion) with manual override available to admins.

[ ] FF5: dedicated_staged_rollouts.emit_stage_tags
    - Adds stage_id/stage_name (or equivalent) tags/labels to key metrics/traces.
    - Must be paired with cardinality limits (allowlist) and sampling settings from telemetry team.

[ ] FF6: dedicated_staged_rollouts.console_timeline
    - Enables Console UI workflow elements + backend endpoints for stage timeline and evidence.

[ ] FF7: dedicated_staged_rollouts.force_override_admin
    - Enables force-promote and hold controls; gated by admin role.
    - Must write explicit audit events with “override=true” + reason.


DB migrations / schema readiness
[ ] M1: Apply rollout plan schema migration (PR-28411)
    - Tables/columns expected:
      - dedicated_pool_rollout_plans (or equivalent)
      - stage definitions (json/blob) with stable stage IDs
      - rollout state machine fields: draft/running/held/aborted/completed
      - optimistic concurrency (etag/version) + idempotency key storage for promote/abort

[ ] M2: Validate forward/backward compatibility
    - Old routing path works when routing_stage_partitioning is OFF.
    - Control plane reads/writes safe under mixed-version service deployment.

[ ] M3: Backfill plan (if required)
    - Decision: DO NOT auto-create rollout plans for all existing Dedicated pools at GA; only create when customer/operator initiates OR when allowlisted account is enabled.
    - If there is any required backfill (e.g., default empty plan rows for allowlisted pools), confirm batch job:
      - Rate limiting (avoid DB hotspots)
      - Idempotent reruns
      - Metrics: rows inserted/updated, failures, duration

[ ] M4: Data retention / cleanup
    - Confirm retention for plan history + audit events aligns with Dedicated/enterprise expectations.
    - Confirm any TTL jobs won’t delete active plan state.


Audit logging & compliance readiness
[ ] A1: Audit events emitted for actions
    - create_plan, update_plan, start_rollout (if separate), promote_stage, abort_rollout, hold_rollout, resume_rollout, force_promote, force_abort (if supported)
    - Required fields: actor, actor_type, account_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, previous_stage, new_stage, override_flag, reason, idempotency_key, request_id, timestamp.

[ ] A2: Audit export pipeline includes new event types (Jira INT-1951)
    - Verify export mapping, indexing, and filtering.
    - Verify enterprise export targets (SIEM) receive events within SLA.

[ ] A3: RBAC verified (Kaitlyn sign-off)
    - Customer admin vs Redwood operator vs Redwood admin distinctions documented.
    - Force-promote requires elevated permission; Console UI must surface warning + require reason.


Telemetry, dashboards, alerting
[ ] T1: Stage-tagged metrics/traces enabled behind emit_stage_tags
    - Verify cardinality guardrails:
      - allowlisted labels only
      - stage_id is stable and bounded (no per-request randomness)
      - sampling applied to traces as needed
    - Confirm hotfix PR-28644 (cardinality regression) is included in release.

[ ] T2: Dashboards deployed (observability-pack PR-631)
    - Required panels:
      - error rate (4xx/5xx) by stage + region
      - p95/p99 latency by stage + region
      - saturation/headroom (GPU util / queue depth)
      - OOM rate / GPU health indicators
      - 429/request drop signals by stage
      - annotations for promotions/aborts/holds

[ ] T3: Alerts configured + routed
    - Gate failure alerts: ticket vs page thresholds agreed with SRE.
    - Ownership:
      - routing partitioning failures -> Routing oncall
      - gate eval pipeline issues -> Policy/Telemetry oncall
      - control plane API errors -> Platform oncall
    - Verify alert noise controls (minimum sample size / windowing).


Performance / reliability gates for GA (go/no-go criteria)
[ ] G1: Integration tests green in CI (PR-28610)
    - Must cover: create plan → start → promote → gate fail → abort/rollback; missing metrics; idempotent promote; concurrent promote requests.

[ ] G2: Canary simulation / load test results archived
    - Demonstrate no regression in:
      - baseline latency at 100% stable stage
      - error rate at stable stage with feature flags OFF
      - routing correctness under multi-region impairment scenario

[ ] G3: SRE sign-off
    - Runbook reviewed and oncall steps are clear.
    - “No promote during incident/high error budget burn” policy documented (even if enforced manually initially).

[ ] G4: Console readiness
    - Gate evidence renders correctly and matches backend queries.
    - Action availability correct (promote blocked when gates fail/unknown, unless override permission).


Canary / rollout plan for production enablement
Phase 0 — Staging verification
[ ] C0.1: Deploy to staging with all flags ON.
[ ] C0.2: Create test Dedicated pool + test plan with default stages: 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% (or replica partitions where applicable).
[ ] C0.3: Validate:
    - promote path
    - abort path
    - hold/resume path
    - missing-metrics behavior shows “Unknown” and blocks promote

Phase 1 — Prod dark launch (no functional change)
[ ] C1.1: Deploy prod services with routing_stage_partitioning OFF.
[ ] C1.2: Enable control_plane_api ON (still safe if no one uses it; RBAC enforced).
[ ] C1.3: Validate API health + DB metrics (connections, query latency).

Phase 2 — Internal canary
[ ] C2.1: Enable dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled for internal Redwood Dedicated pools only.
[ ] C2.2: Enable routing_stage_partitioning for those pools.
[ ] C2.3: Enable emit_stage_tags for those pools (watch cardinality).
[ ] C2.4: Run controlled staged rollout of a harmless change (e.g., routing policy toggle) and verify promotion annotations + gate evaluation.

Phase 3 — Limited external beta (design partners)
[ ] C3.1: Confirm allowlisted accounts/pools (tracked via INT-1933).
[ ] C3.2: Enable per account/pool (avoid partial region exposure unless explicitly desired).
[ ] C3.3: Provide customer comms: expectations, how to interpret holds/aborts, escalation path.
[ ] C3.4: Monitor for known failure mode: canary partition starving capacity and causing 429 spikes (SUP-28522 learnings).

Phase 4 — GA enablement
[ ] C4.1: Default availability: staged rollouts feature available to all Dedicated accounts (or tiered rollout by customer segment per Product).
[ ] C4.2: Confirm support readiness: macros, oncall routing, escalation policy.


Customer + internal comms plan
[ ] COM1: Release notes drafted (internal + customer-facing)
    - Include: what staged rollouts are, default stage templates, what gates are evaluated, what “hold/abort” means.

[ ] COM2: Internal enablement
    - #eng-oncall playbook update + short training
    - TAM/CS brief (what customers will see in Console; how to request enablement)

[ ] COM3: Customer announcement
    - Target segment: Dedicated admins/operators
    - Include: how to request enablement (if allowlist), docs link, limitations (no arbitrary custom metrics in v1)

[ ] COM4: Change management packet for regulated customers (if needed)
    - Audit event coverage summary
    - Retention/export statement
    - RBAC overview


Rollback plan (must be executable in <15 minutes)
Principles
- Prefer flag rollback over code rollback.
- Rollback should revert routing behavior first (protect SLOs), then disable promotion actions, then reduce telemetry surface.

Rollback triggers (examples)
- Elevated 429s or sustained queue depth spike in canary stage indicating capacity starvation.
- Routing misassignment across stage partitions or region bleed.
- Gate evaluation instability causing repeated false aborts/holds.
- Telemetry cardinality incident.

Rollback steps (ordered)
[ ] R1: Disable routing_stage_partitioning in prod for affected pools/accounts (or globally if unclear scope).
    - Expected effect: all traffic routes to stable partition/path; staged rollout becomes no-op.

[ ] R2: Disable gate_eval_v1 (if gate system suspected)
    - Expected effect: promotion blocks or reverts to manual-only behavior depending on implementation; confirm with Platform.

[ ] R3: Disable console_timeline (if Console endpoints failing / confusing)
    - Expected effect: hide staged rollout workflow; prevent customer actions.

[ ] R4: Disable emit_stage_tags (if telemetry cardinality issues)
    - Note: dashboards will lose stage breakdown; keep baseline pool dashboards.

[ ] R5: Disable master flag dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled

[ ] R6: If DB migration issue suspected
    - DO NOT attempt down-migration during incident.
    - Mitigation: feature-flag off + hotfix forward.

[ ] R7: Post-rollback validation
    - Confirm pool-level SLOs returning to baseline (latency, error, saturation).
    - Confirm audit events still emitted for any manual actions taken during incident.


Open items / final sign-offs (must be checked before GA)
[ ] S1: SRE (Rafael/Sean): alert routing + runbook sign-off.
[ ] S2: Security (Kaitlyn): RBAC + audit log completeness sign-off.
[ ] S3: Telemetry (Logan/Allison): cardinality controls + dashboard templates sign-off.
[ ] S4: Routing (Mina): multi-region impairment behavior sign-off.
[ ] S5: Console (Chloe/Jada): customer-facing UX copy + evidence rendering sign-off.
[ ] S6: Release Eng (Connor): release train slot confirmed + staged rollout of flags scheduled.

Notes / lessons learned to carry forward
- Capacity fragmentation risk is highest for small Dedicated pools; ensure validation rules block stages that would create under-sized partitions.
- Missing metrics must not silently pass gates; fail-closed with explicit override + audit is the accepted v1 stance.
- Canary stage can create unexpected effective capacity reduction; watch for 429 spikes and queue depth growth within first 10 minutes of canary enablement.
